findings.title: The AI context picker omits project data that the send path adds anyway

evidence.detail: Send prepends selected blocks; preview shows only those blocks.
The first send independently appends all entity summaries to the system prompt.
Raw entity loads bypass the SDK's AI inclusion filtering.
The SDK explicitly distinguishes raw entity loads from privacy-filtered GetAiContextAsync.

findings.trigger: Send a first chat message with no Context items selected, including a project with entities marked never include in AI.
findings.impact: Names, roles, types and some custom field values enter the provider request despite the empty picker/preview. With a cloud provider, this is an unintended disclosure of project details; it is not a claim that every entity body is sent.
findings.recommendation: Assemble one authoritative request for preview and send. Respect per-entry/per-section exclusions and remove the legacy automatic roster from the chat path.
findings.validation: Capture a fake provider request with the picker empty and an excluded entity. Assert its unique marker appears in neither system nor user messages; preview should account for every context block.

findings.title: AI chat conversations survive a switch to a different project

evidence.detail: Conversation history is instance state and clears only on explicit Clear.
The system prompt and project roster are built only on the first message.
Controllers are cached by extension and view, with no project/book component.

findings.trigger: Chat about project A, open project B in the same application session, then return to AI Chat and send a message.
findings.impact: The old history and roster can accompany a request about the new project, contaminating answers and sending project A details again.
findings.recommendation: Scope conversation state to project/book identity or explicitly reset it during a coordinated workspace change. Cancel active requests before switching their owning context.
findings.validation: Use two synthetic projects with distinctive markers; switch projects and inspect the next provider request and displayed history. Test an in-flight response during the switch too.

findings.title: Character knowledge caches can write one project's data into another

evidence.detail: The lifetime cache is keyed only by character ID.
The output directory is resolved from the currently open project on every access.
A cache hit returns before reading the current project's file.
Save writes cached character data under the current project root.

findings.trigger: Open two copies/forks of a project that preserve character IDs, loading knowledge in A before switching to B and updating that character.
findings.impact: B can receive A's cached scene knowledge. Distinct project roots are not sufficient isolation because the cache key ignores them.
findings.recommendation: Key cached records and locks by canonical project identity plus character ID; capture that identity for the whole read-modify-write operation and invalidate on context changes.
findings.validation: A fake host with switchable project roots should load different knowledge for the same character ID and never write A's marker to B. Include a delayed write spanning a switch.

findings.title: Cancellation does not reach every AI provider or model-loading phase

evidence.detail: The model-load semaphore and HTTP calls have no caller cancellation token.
Model loading completes before the request's linked token is created.
Copilot GenerateAsync receives no caller token.
Anthropic GenerateAsync receives no caller token; the client creates its own CTS.

findings.trigger: Cancel while LM Studio is loading a model, or cancel an extension workflow through its supplied token while Anthropic/Copilot is generating.
findings.impact: The model-load probe remains pending after cancellation. The other two provider paths also disconnect caller cancellation from their underlying operation, so paid/slow work can continue after the workflow is cancelled. The dedicated chat Cancel button additionally calls AiService.Cancel, which mitigates that particular UI path.
findings.recommendation: Thread the caller token through model discovery/loading, semaphore waits and every provider request. Own cancellation per operation and dispose linked sources in finally.
findings.validation: ai-probe reproduces cancellation during a delayed fake model listing. Add provider contract tests for pre-cancelled and mid-stream cancellation, including concurrent independent requests.

findings.title: Concurrent AI requests share mutable model and cancellation state

evidence.detail: UseRequestModel temporarily mutates shared provider clients.
ModelScope.Dispose restores its saved value regardless of overlapping scopes.
CLI chunk callbacks and _cts are also shared across requests.

findings.trigger: Overlap chat with analysis/critique, or select a second model while the first request is active.
findings.impact: An isolated interleaving of the actual model scopes ends with default model 'first' instead of 'original'. Shared callbacks and cancellation pointers create related cross-request hazards; those races were identified in code, not separately driven through a live provider.
findings.recommendation: Capture immutable request options and pass model/callback/token directly into provider methods. Serialize providers that support only one prompt, with a provider-level queue rather than relying on each caller to cooperate.
findings.validation: ai-probe reproduces out-of-order scope disposal. Add overlapping request tests proving model restoration, stream ownership and cancelling one request does not cancel another.

findings.title: An SSE event with no choices aborts an otherwise valid AI reply

evidence.detail: FirstOrDefault on an empty choices array yields an undefined JsonElement; TryGetProperty then throws.
Only JsonException is caught, not that InvalidOperationException.

findings.trigger: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint includes an empty choices array, such as a usage-only event, after text deltas.
findings.impact: A completed-looking answer is followed by an error and is not committed as a successful assistant response. A fake SSE stream reproduces the exact exception without calling any external provider.
findings.recommendation: Validate choices is an array with an object element before reading delta, and process terminal/usage events independently of content deltas.
findings.validation: Run ai-probe. Add streams with empty choices, usage-only events, terminal events without delta, malformed events and normal completion; preserve all preceding text.

findings.title: Chat budgets selected context but not the complete conversation

evidence.detail: Budgeting applies to the blocks passed to Assemble.
Each selected context is prepended to the stored user turn.
The entire unbounded conversation is sent again.
Every stored message enters the request payload.

findings.trigger: Keep a long chat open and repeatedly include a scene/chapter in the context picker.
findings.impact: Repeated context accumulates in previous turns, outside the preview's displayed budget. Request sizes and provider cost grow until a context-window rejection, despite the selected-block preview appearing within budget.
findings.recommendation: Budget the final message list, reserve output space, avoid storing duplicate context as permanent user prose, and clearly report older turns omitted from an over-limit request. A bounded history policy is sufficient; no new AI feature is needed.
findings.validation: Drive many turns through a fake provider with a small configured budget. Assert full payload size stays bounded and the preview reflects the actual final context.

findings.title: Clear Chat can be undone by an in-flight response

evidence.detail: ClearChatAsync clears collections without cancelling/awaiting active generation.
The pending send later appends to the same collections.
Generating state disables Send but not Clear.

findings.trigger: Press Clear while an AI reply is streaming and let the request finish.
findings.impact: Old content can repopulate the cleared conversation. The resulting history can begin with an assistant response whose user turn was deleted.
findings.recommendation: Cancel and retire the generation before clearing, or guard completion/stream callbacks with a conversation generation ID.
findings.validation: Delay fake provider completion, clear, then release completion. Neither streamed nor final text from the old generation should appear in the new history.

findings.title: Copilot receives the full history inside an already persistent session

evidence.detail: Every call flattens all supplied messages into one prompt.
GenerateAsync reuses the same ACP session across prompts.
The session resets only when explicitly requested.

findings.trigger: Send several chat turns through Copilot, or use another AI workflow between chat turns.
findings.impact: Conversation content is resent into a session that already retains prior turns, and the same client/session is shared across workflows. This increases duplicated context and mixes unrelated task history.
findings.recommendation: Choose one history owner: send only new turns to a dedicated chat session, or start an isolated session for each complete transcript. Give one-shot analysis workflows independent sessions.
findings.validation: Fake the ACP peer and record session IDs/prompt payloads over two chat turns and one analysis call. Check that each prior turn is represented once and workflows are isolated.

findings.title: Context preview mislabels blocks that share a display name

evidence.detail: Dropped block headings are turned into a set.
Every block with that heading is then marked dropped, including one that was kept.

findings.trigger: Include two context entries with the same heading, where only one fits the budget.
findings.impact: The preview can say a block was dropped while the actual request includes it. The isolated probe reports firstContentSent=true but firstShownAsKept=false.
findings.recommendation: Track kept/dropped decisions by stable block identity or assembly result index, not display labels. Produce preview and send from that same result.
findings.validation: Run ai-probe; add duplicate-heading cases with different sizes and weights and assert every preview row matches the included text.

findings.title: AI Assistant releases bypass its existing test suite and float the SDK source

evidence.detail: The only workflow is tag-triggered release.
SDK checkout has no ref and follows the host default branch.
Release restores/builds/packages without dotnet test.
Minimum host remains 3.0.0 independently of the selected SDK revision.

findings.trigger: Tag an AI Assistant release after changes to providers, dictation or the host SDK.
findings.impact: The 100 passing local tests are not a release prerequisite. Rebuilding the same tag can compile against a different SDK revision; declared compatibility may then be broader than what was tested. No specific old-host load failure is asserted here.
findings.recommendation: Run existing tests on PRs and before packaging, pin the SDK revision used for a release, and validate the declared minimum host against the SDK members actually used.
findings.validation: Introduce a failing provider test and assert release cannot proceed; rebuild the same tag and compare SDK revision/manifest. Test loading on the minimum supported host.

findings.title: Cached webview controllers remain callable after their extension is disabled

evidence.detail: SetEnabledAsync changes extension state without retiring controllers.
GetController returns a cached instance before checking IsEnabled.
Uninstall does not clear cached controllers either.

findings.trigger: Open an extension view, disable/uninstall it, then deliver a queued or stale webview message; re-enable can also reuse that old controller.
findings.impact: The disabled instance can still receive work and retain event handlers/state. Disabling an extension does not consistently retire its active UI controllers.
findings.recommendation: Check enabled state before cache lookup; dispose and unsubscribe controllers on disable/uninstall and create fresh ones on re-enable. Include workspace ownership in controller lifecycle where needed.
findings.validation: A backend contract test should open a fake controller, disable it, send another message and assert zero invocations. Verify disposal, notification unsubscription and fresh re-enable state.

findings.title: Mobile has no lifecycle flush for edits waiting on autosave

evidence.detail: The Window is created without Stopped/Deactivated save wiring.
No native background lifecycle override is installed.
Scene autosave waits 2,000 milliseconds.
Desktop close flushing depends on onBeforeClose, absent from the mobile shim.

findings.trigger: Type and immediately background/lock the app before its debounce fires; the OS later terminates the backgrounded process.
findings.impact: The last edits have no explicit native lifecycle path to flush. File coordination protects a write that has started, but does not start the renderer's pending save. This is a confirmed wiring gap; actual loss timing requires an iPhone/iPad test.
findings.recommendation: Connect scene/window background transitions to the existing pending-write/editor flush, with a bounded native background task and acknowledgement. Preserve a recoverable draft if a provider cannot finish before suspension.
findings.validation: On a real device: type a unique marker, immediately lock or switch away, terminate after backgrounding and reopen. Repeat with cloud-only files, offline mode, research notes and an unresolved conflict.

findings.title: Mobile folder grants accumulate without a balanced release path

evidence.detail: Picking a folder starts a security-scoped resource.
Repeated picks overwrite Active[path] without stopping its previous grant.
Resolving bookmarks starts additional grants.
endProjectAccess is exposed, but there are no renderer call sites.

findings.trigger: Open/switch among many external projects, or repeatedly pick the same folder in one session.
findings.impact: Native scope starts have no balanced release during the session, and overwritten entries can no longer be released by their original ownership record. Apple explicitly requires balancing starts and stops; eventual device resource failure has not been measured here.
findings.recommendation: Represent grants as reference-counted leases owned by operations/projects, release old leases after switching, and balance all failure paths after a successful start.
findings.validation: Instrument start/stop counts in a macOS/iOS test build; repeatedly open/close/reselect folders and resolve recents. Counts and retained scope records should return to the active-project baseline.

findings.title: Mobile path repair can redirect an external project to a different local project

evidence.detail: Any stored path containing /Documents/ is eligible for local-container remapping.
The replacement is accepted when a same-suffix directory exists.
The candidate is checked for project presence, then its path is persisted; identity is not compared.

findings.trigger: An unavailable external project path ends in /Documents/Foo, while the app's own Documents/Foo holds a different project.
findings.impact: The recent-project entry can be silently repointed to the unrelated local project. A container migration heuristic is being applied to paths whose provenance is unknown.
findings.recommendation: Restrict container repair to previously recorded app-owned paths and compare stable project identity before updating recents. Treat external/bookmarked paths separately.
findings.validation: Add resolver tests for old-container paths, external paths with matching suffixes and two distinct project IDs. On-device, upgrade the app and verify genuine container relocation still works.

findings.title: A failed mobile bridge delivery can leave requests pending forever

evidence.detail: The backend pump exits on read failure without a renderer connection-state message.
JavaScript evaluation errors are logged then swallowed, dropping the message.
Host promises remain in a pending map until a matching response arrives.
hostCall has no readiness handshake, deadline or disconnection rejection.

findings.trigger: A host result or RPC chunk cannot be delivered during WebView startup/reload, or the in-process transport stops.
findings.impact: Pickers/saves can wait indefinitely; a dropped byte chunk may also corrupt RPC framing. No recovery hook for WebKit process termination was found, but MAUI's exact default behavior must be checked on-device.
findings.recommendation: Queue delivery until the JS bridge acknowledges readiness, propagate connection failures, reject pending operations on teardown, and rebuild the channel with an epoch after reload. Do not replay non-idempotent writes blindly.
findings.validation: Inject one EvaluateJavaScript failure and one pump read failure. Assert calls settle with an actionable error and a new channel can reconnect without duplicating a write. Exercise WebView termination on a device/simulator.

findings.title: Native mobile regressions are first compiled in the release workflow

evidence.detail: The web job builds the mobile web bundle, not the MAUI/iOS host.
The mobile project is intentionally absent from the desktop solution.
Native mobile compilation occurs in the signed IPA release job.
Mobile UI tests use Electron with a mobile flag, not WKWebView/native host behavior.

findings.trigger: A PR changes native picker/bridge/lifecycle code or a web API that differs in WKWebView.
findings.impact: Green desktop CI cannot establish that the iOS host compiles or that the native bridge works. The shared UI tests are useful but do not exercise file-provider grants, suspension, native presentation or AOT behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add a macOS simulator compile/smoke gate for existing mobile paths, and run a short signed-device acceptance checklist before release. Keep the desktop coverage gate unchanged.
findings.validation: A deliberately broken native symbol must fail a PR check. On the real native build, open a fixture project, edit/save/relaunch, pick/import/share a file and exercise dictation permissions.

findings.title: Help screenshots dominate the mobile application's initial JavaScript

evidence.detail: All manual images are converted to base64 strings in one virtual module.
The help component statically imports those image strings.
The shell statically imports HelpOverlay, keeping it in the initial graph.

findings.trigger: Launch the application, even when Help is never opened.
findings.impact: The audited mobile build emits 16,129.00 kB of initial JS (10,569.57 kB gzip). Eleven source screenshots total 9,512,185 bytes, about 12.68 MB when base64 encoded. This is a measured bundle-size issue; no claim about device launch milliseconds is made.
findings.recommendation: Serve packaged screenshots as separate static assets and lazy-load Help plus its manual content. Keep offline help intact and avoid downloading anything at runtime.
findings.validation: Rebuild and compare entry chunk bytes, then measure cold launch, JS parse time and peak memory on the oldest supported iPhone/iPad and desktop. Verify every help image still loads offline.

findings.title: AI streaming resends the entire accumulated reply for every chunk

evidence.detail: Each token appends to a growing observable string.
Every string change serializes full streaming and thinking strings.
The view updates the full streamed reply on state messages.

findings.trigger: Generate a long response or long reasoning stream, especially with small provider chunks.
findings.impact: Bridge payload work grows quadratically with answer length. For a synthetic 12,000-character reply delivered in 3,000 four-character chunks, the repeated text alone totals 18,006,000 characters rather than 12,000. That is protocol arithmetic, not a measured latency benchmark.
findings.recommendation: Send incremental deltas or throttle full-state snapshots to animation-frame/short intervals. Keep a final authoritative response and handle cancellation without replaying every intermediate string.
findings.validation: Replay a fixed synthetic stream and record bytes, UI update count and responsiveness. Final text and thinking must match exactly for normal completion and cancellation.

findings.title: Three oversized renderer functions remain in the quality scan

evidence.detail: Aislop reports BinderChapters at 183 lines.
Aislop reports ExtensionStore at 178 lines.
Aislop reports LayerPanel at 346 lines.

findings.trigger: Make future fixes in binder interactions, extension store state or map layer controls.
findings.impact: These mixed responsibilities make bounded changes harder to reason about. The installed scanner gives 100/100 while reporting three non-fixable warnings, so the score must not be read as zero findings or proof of behavioral correctness.
findings.recommendation: Extract coherent state transitions and repeated subviews when addressing their next behavior fix. Preserve public behavior and add only tests for meaningful state boundaries; do not split functions merely to game a line threshold.
findings.validation: Re-run aislop on the touched files and relevant interaction tests. Swift was unsupported by this scan; native code still needs its own review.

findings.title: The gallery's AI Assistant description advertises only two of its providers

evidence.detail: Store description mentions only LM Studio and GitHub Copilot CLI.
The extension manifest describes Ollama, compatible services, Anthropic and Claude CLI as well.

findings.trigger: Browse the extension gallery before installing AI Assistant.
findings.impact: The discovery surface undersells existing supported connections and omits several established capabilities. The underlying implementation is present; this is metadata drift.
findings.recommendation: Update the short gallery description from the extension's current supported capabilities and add a lightweight manifest/gallery consistency check for IDs and core metadata.
findings.validation: Validate gallery JSON and compare the rendered store card with the extension manifest. This requires no provider or product feature change.

checks.detail: All eight source checks passed. Locale check: 0 missing, untranslated, placeholder or spelling failures; dead-key candidates remain advisory.
75 tests passed. Initial sandbox process-spawn failure was resolved by running the same tests with approved execution.
Web assets compiled; bundle-size and mixed static/dynamic import warnings recorded. This is not a native iOS build.
100 passed, 4 skipped. No installed extension was changed. A generated-code CS0162 warning was emitted.
Four isolated probes reproduced empty-choices SSE failure, uncancelled model loading, model-scope restoration race and preview heading collision.
Registry advisory query: 0 production dependency vulnerabilities reported. Does not prove the application has no vulnerabilities.
NuGet reported no vulnerable backend packages in the restored dependency graph.
100/100, 1,638 supported files, 2 unsupported Swift files, three non-fixable function-length warnings. No .aislop/config.yaml was present; no configuration was changed.

The generated Publish link fixture creates an event-handler attribute and executes it on mouseover in headless Chromium. An independent hidden Electron probe rejected an opaque-origin fetch of a synthetic project file; that suspected exposure was excluded from findings.
